Not applicable: one trial, so there is no between-study variance to estimate.

Nothing is pooled: one trial. This is not a withheld estimate -- the value stands and is clear Outcomes' own.

Why this pool stands. The estimate STANDS, and it is one trial's result rather than a synthesis -- which the card says, with k=1. HR 0.87 (0.79 to 0.96) is clear Outcomes' own registered Cox analysis, digit for digit, over its registered primary outcome: 'Number of Participants With First Occurrence of Four Component Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (mace)', defined by its registry record as 'death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization, as assessed in a time-to first-event analysis'. Its counts are the registry's own: 819 of 6,992 against 927 of 6,978. And k=1 is correct rather than a shortfall. Of the four registrations this page includes, only clear Outcomes registers a cardiovascular-event primary. Clear Harmony's registered primaries are safety endpoints -- treatment-emergent adverse events and events of special interest, at 52 weeks. Clear Serenity's is percent change in ldl-c at week 12, a laboratory value. Neither can enter a mace estimate, so leaving them out is right; what is missing is any statement that they were left out or why.

Three things a reader should know, none of which overturns the estimate. (1) one of the four included registrations is not a bempedoic acid trial at all. NCT02973841 is 'Sono-ease', a forty-patient device study of internal jugular vein cannulation whose registered primary outcome is 'complications rate'. It sits in this page's own include list. It carries no data record, so it touches no number here -- but it is the second wrong registration found in this corpus in one session, after NCT02583191 turned out to be a German treatment-satisfaction study on DOAC_CANCER_VTE. A registration that names an unrelated trial is invisible to every check that asks only whether an id is present and unique. (2) the published-comparison STEP compares this estimate against itself. The page's benchmark database holds exactly one entry for this outcome: 'clear Outcomes bempedoic acid vs placebo', Nissen 2023, HR 0.87 (0.79 to 0.96), k=1, n=13,970. That IS the trial whose result is on the card. A comparison of a number with itself agrees perfectly and establishes nothing, and the agreement should not be read as external corroboration. The honest denominator here is zero: no independent synthesis of this estimand is recorded on this page. (3) a single trial is not a synthesis. Nothing here is pooled, there is no heterogeneity to report, and the interval is clear Outcomes' own. The value of this page over reading the trial report is the provenance chain, not the statistics.

Abstract

Question. Does bempedoic acid reduce major cardiovascular events in statin-intolerant patients? One trial answers this; the other three registrations on this page measure something else, and one of them is not a bempedoic acid trial.1

Methods. ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 and PubMed (ncbi e-utilities esearch) were searched; estimates were pooled under single study; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE.2

Results. Four-component mace: cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization: hazard ratio 0.87 (0.79 to 0.96) across 1 trials; and certainty of the evidence was low.3

Refused: the Background sentence of the abstract. Background is argument -- why this question matters -- and no arrangement of the quantities this object holds yields it. It is emitted only from an authored field and there is no composition path for it here4
Refused: the Conclusions sentence of the abstract. A conclusion is argument -- what a reader should now believe -- and it is emitted only from an authored field. Composing one from the estimate would be this renderer telling the reader what to conclude, which no field supports5

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: Does bempedoic acid reduce major cardiovascular events in statin-intolerant patients? One trial answers this; the other three registrations on this page measure something else, and one of them is not a bempedoic acid trial. It pools 1 randomised trial, against placebo. The outcome pooled is Four-component mace: cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization.

[Draft] The evidence identified on this question is 1 randomised trial (NCT02993406), pooled here at 0.87 (95% CI 0.79 to 0.96) for primary. Certainty in that estimate is rated LOW. Which of those unresolved points makes the question worth asking now is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] No search for published syntheses is recorded on this object. Whether those differences warrant a new synthesis rather than citing the existing one is the author's judgement.3

Methods — search

Searches were executed in ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 2026-08-18 with the query, verbatim: condition="hypercholesterolemia OR dyslipidemia OR cardiovascular disease"; intervention="bempedoic acid"; study_type=interventional; phase=[PHASE3,PHASE4]; count_total=true; page_size=60. It returned 21 record(s).1

Searches were executed in PubMed (ncbi e-utilities esearch) on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: (bempedoic acid[tiab] or etc-1002[tiab] OR Nexletol[tiab] OR Nilemdo[tiab]) and (cardiovascular[tiab] or mace[tiab] OR "major adverse cardiovascular events"[tiab]) and (randomized controlled trial[pt] OR randomised[tiab] OR randomized[tiab]). It returned 50 record(s).2

Primary trials. No bibliographic search for primary trials was run. The 1 included trial was identified by reading named registration on the dates recorded on each entry. This object's verification rests on ClinicalTrials.gov protocol and results records, read 2026-08-18. This review does not claim that the value was checked against the journal report; it is the registry's own analysis. The bar this object had to clear is not recorded.3

Methods — synthesis

Methodological decisions follow not recorded on the page this object was built from, version not recorded on the page this object was built from, and the sections relied on are listed in the object rather than cited generically.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (22 August 2019 version, as reproduced in the Cochrane Handbook), following Higgins JPT, Savovic J, Page MJ, Elbers RG, Sterne JAC. Chapter 8: Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial. In: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1. A result, not a study -- Handbook 8.2: 'risk of bias is assessed for a specific result'. Every judgement below names its outcome. 1 result-level assessments were made. A domain that cannot be judged from the registration and the published report is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.2

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.3

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1, Chapter 14: Completing 'Summary of findings' tables and grading the certainty of the evidence. HIGH for a body of randomised evidence, then rated down with reasons. 1 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated UP. Rating up for large effect or dose-response applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.4

Refused: the model/estimator sentence for four-component mace: cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization -- the model or estimator is recorded as a null marker rather than a value5
Refused: the claim that records were screened in duplicate -- and this topic owes one rather than merely lacking one: No second independent screen was run for this topic. This is recorded as owed rather than described: the remedy is to RUN one, and writing a duplicate-screening sentence without one would be the defect this whole exercise exists to prevent.6
Refused: the claim that the review methods were prespecified before data collection. This refusal is permanent and is not a gap to be filled. A protocol specified before data collection is a historical fact about the past and cannot be created retrospectively. Writing one now and calling it prespecified would invalidate every other refusal on these pages, because a reader who caught it would be right to disbelieve all of them. Eligibility criteria were derived post hoc from the trials and the methodological authority, and the derivation is recorded element by element in `screening.eligibility_provenance` with the source of each. Mecir R107 permits post-hoc eligibility criteria provided they are declared as such. They are declared, here and on the page, and the page says 'derived, post hoc' in its heading.7

The pooled hazard ratio for four-component mace: cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization was 0.87 (0.79 to 0.96) across 1 trials, against placebo.1

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is a result, not a study -- Handbook 8.2: 'risk of bias is assessed for a specific result'. Every judgement below names its outcome.1

No result in this review can reach LOW risk of bias on the evidence we can reach, and that is a fact about our access rather than about the trials. The two domains that would distinguish LOW from some concerns need documents this review does not hold: D1 needs allocation concealment and baseline data, which are in neither the registration nor the published abstract; D5 needs the trial's statistical analysis plan, which is not held for any trial. Some concerns is therefore the ceiling, not a finding. A trial rated some concerns here may well be at low risk of bias -- we cannot show it, and we do not imply the opposite. Retrieving each trial's full published report and its statistical analysis plan or protocol. Until then the rating is bounded by what we read, and the bound is reported rather than the reader inferring it.2

A domain that cannot be judged from the registration and the published report is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect.3

A second, independent assessment was obtained from: gpt-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`4

The assessment above was made by: Claude Opus 5 (anthropic family) -- the assessment above5

How the second assessor was asked: Blind, from scripts/second_assessor_prompt.py. The prompt is assembled from an ALLOW-LIST of registry-sourced factual fields and refuses to send if any RoB 2 verdict word appears in the assembled text. The second assessor was not shown this assessment and was not asked whether it agreed.6

The disagreement rate, reported as disagreement because agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing: 3 of 6 judgements -- 50.0%. Reported as disagreement: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing.7

Where they disagree, by domain: D1 0 of 1 disagree, D2 0 of 1 disagree, D3 1 of 1 disagree, D4 0 of 1 disagree, D5 1 of 1 disagree and overall 1 of 1 disagree.8

Every disagreement, named: NCT02993406 on Four-component mace: cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization D3: assessor 1 LOW, assessor 2 NO_INFORMATION; NCT02993406 on Four-component mace: cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization D5: assessor 1 NO_INFORMATION, assessor 2 LOW; NCT02993406 on Four-component mace: cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or coronary revascularization overall: assessor 1 NO_INFORMATION, assessor 2 SOME_CONCERNS.9

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE. HIGH for a body of randomised evidence, then rated down with reasons.1

No domain is rated UP. Rating up for large effect or dose-response applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.2

risk_of_bias -1 inconsistency +0 indirectness +0 imprecision -1 publication_bias +03

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: D1 on 1 result(s), D2 on 1 result(s), D5 on 1 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.4

Not one reaches LOW -- D5 cannot, because no trial's statistical analysis plan is held, and D1 cannot, because allocation concealment is in neither the registration nor this object. 1 have at least one domain at no information. This is a limit on what we can reach, not a finding against the trials.; inconsistency: not rated down -- k = 1: inconsistency cannot be assessed with a single contributing result, and not assessable is recorded rather than 'no inconsistency'.; indirectness: not rated down -- The contributing results share one endpoint definition, verified by reading each trial's registered text rather than by comparing names.; imprecision: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s) -- k = 1. Note on registration

Protocol status. Prespecified: False. A protocol specified before data collection is a historical fact about the past and cannot be created retrospectively. Writing one now and calling it prespecified would invalidate every other refusal on these pages, because a reader who caught it would be right to disbelieve all of them.1

Eligibility criteria were derived post hoc from the trials and the methodological authority, and the derivation is recorded element by element in `screening.eligibility_provenance` with the source of each.2

Authority: Mecir R107 permits post-hoc eligibility criteria provided they are declared as such. They are declared, here and on the page, and the page says 'derived, post hoc' in its heading.3

No PROSPERO registration or protocol record is held on this object. That is not the same as knowing this review was not registered, and neither claim is made. It is recorded here as an absence so that a reader does not have to infer it from silence.4

The withholding question, asked at every rank

does this trial report, AT ANY RANK -- primary, secondary or other -- an outcome matching what the included trial reports as its primary?

Reading only registered PRIMARIES is how a poolable outcome one rank down goes unseen. Two of the three MACE-matching outcomes found here sit at SECONDARY rank and a primaries-only screen would have missed both.

Correction — NCT02666664

The recorded reason reads: 'its registered primaries are SAFETY outcomes -- treatment-emergent adverse events and events of special interest -- not cardiovascular events.' That is FACTUALLY WRONG. NCT02666664 registers THIRTEEN primary outcomes and the SECOND is 'Percentage of Participants With Adjudicated Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event'. It has a MACE primary.

How it happened: The object stores `registered_primary_measure` as a SCALAR holding ONE of the trial's thirteen primaries -- the first, TEAEs -- and the exclusion reason was written by characterising all primaries from that single value. A scalar field standing for a list is how the other twelve became invisible.

Verdict: EXCLUDE is still correct. The failing limb is POPULATION, not OUTCOME: this is CLEAR Harmony, in high-cardiovascular-risk patients on maximally tolerated statin therapy, whereas the review's population limb is statin-intolerant patients.

Class: A correct verdict reached by broken reasoning. It passed every outcome-based check because the outcome -- exclusion -- was right. Only reading the REASON against the registry caught it, and only because the withholding question is asked at every rank rather than at the primary alone.

Analysis output — ABSENT_AND_THAT_IS_THE_FINDING

k=1 and nothing was pooled, so there is NO model call to quote, NO pooled estimate, NO heterogeneity and NO package version. This is not a missing artefact; it is the correct state for a topic with no synthesis.

What stands instead: HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.79 to 0.96)
Provenance: CLEAR Outcomes' OWN registry-posted analysis, NOT a synthesis result computed here
Hazard Ratio (HR) 0.87, CI 0.79 - 0.96, statistical method Log Rank, p=0.004

Heterogeneity: Undefined: no between-study variance was estimated because no model was run.
What would change it: An estimand shared by two or more included trials. Where k is already above 1 and nothing pooled, the obstacle is the ESTIMAND rather than the evidence base, and this field must say which.

Published-meta comparison — PENDING_EXTERNAL_RESOLUTION

Denominator: —. The honest denominator here is ZERO, and that is a finding rather than a shortfall. The only benchmark this page holds for this estimand is CLEAR Outcomes itself -- the single trial whose result the card serves. A comparison of a number with itself agrees perfectly and establishes nothing, and that agreement must not be read as external corroboration. No INDEPENDENT synthesis of this estimand is recorded.

Explicitly not done: CITATION-STRING MATCHING. It would produce a comparison-shaped answer tonight and it is not identity: two syntheses citing the same trial under different labels would read as different, and the same label on different trials as the same. That is the substitution class this project audits for.

Blocked on: lane 2 registration-id resolution
